newsitem.title: USA: Peter Roth named Fox Entertainment president.
newsitem.headline: Peter Roth named Fox Entertainment president.

text.p: Peter Roth, president of News Corp.'s Twentieth Century Fox Television, has been named president of the Fox Entertainment Group. He replaces John Matoian, who has resigned.
Roth will now oversee all Fox Broadcasting Co. programming, scheduling and marketing.

Fox said Roth led the Fox studio to its most successful pilot-selling season in its history in the 1996-97 season. He is credited with the success of the science-fiction drama, "The X-Files," which runs on the Fox network, as well as "Chicago Hope" and "Picket Fences," both seen on CBS.

David Hill, president and chief operating officer of Fox Television, said in a statement that John Matoian "felt the time was not right for him personally to continue that level of commitment" necessary for Fox to build upon its successes.
The management shift leaves open the 20th Century Fox presidency.

Fox was not available to comment, but published reports in the entertainment press listed former CBS Entertainment President Peter Tortorici, former CBS executive Andy Hill, and 20th Century Fox Executive Vice President Gary Newman as likely candidates.
